column8: Layout does not adapt at the 768px tablet breakpoint, leaving dead space down the right side
column9: 1) Open bluntly.ph 2) Set the viewport to 768 x 1024 3) Observe the headline, search bar and featured card 4) Compare the space used against the full viewport width
column10: At 768px the hero should use the width available — copy on one side, featured card beside it — as the container and the header already do at that width.
column11: Content stays in a single narrow column as if still on mobile while the container is already 72rem wide and the header has switched to its desktop form, so roughly the right-hand third of the viewport is empty. The search bar itself renders correctly and is not clipped.
column24: Filed from Coverage Checklist row 53, which was logged as BUG-XXX. Root cause: the hero grid split at lg (1024px) while the container was already max-w-72rem and the header switched to desktop at md (768px), so a tablet got one narrow column stranded in a wide shell. The split now starts at md. Regression test added in e2e/responsive.spec.ts — confirmed it fails without the fix (hero copy spans 720px of a 768px viewport) and passes with it.

column8: Landscape mobile shows the same non-adapting layout, with some words clipped
column9: 1) Open bluntly.ph on a phone 2) Rotate to landscape 3) Observe the hero layout and text
column10: The layout should reflow to use the landscape width rather than keeping the portrait column.
column11: Same dead-space / non-adapting behaviour as BUG-027, and the layout feels too wide overall with some words appearing clipped.
column24: Filed from Coverage Checklist row 55, logged as BUG-XXX and tentatively noted as possibly the same problem as row 53. It is: a landscape phone lands in the same 768px-and-up band, so the md split fixes both. Retest the clipped-words observation separately — if words are still clipped after this, that is a distinct bug and should get its own row rather than being reopened here.

column8: Proof-of-purchase receipts were stored in a PUBLIC storage bucket and their location was returned by anonymous-readable API responses
column9: 1) Sign in and submit a review with a proof-of-purchase image 2) Read the object URL the upload endpoint returns 3) Sign out entirely and request that URL 4) Separately, publish any review carrying a receipt and call GET /api/v1/reviews/{id} and GET /api/v1/reviews/{id}/versions with no credentials
column10: A receipt is evidence for moderator evaluation of the earn_eligible gate (PRD FR-3, FR-9). It must never be retrievable from storage without authorization, and no anonymous response should disclose its location.
column11: Step 3 returned HTTP 200 and the receipt image. Steps 4 returned receipt_url on ReviewOut and an embedded receipt_url inside every review_versions snapshot, both readable with no credentials once the review was published.
column19: Withheld: reproducing this defect requires a real customer's receipt. Evidence is in the commit and the migration script output.
column24: Root cause: one function served two audiences. upload_review_photo() and POST /reviews/photo were documented as returning a URL suitable for photo_url OR receipt_url, so the caller's convention rather than the server decided whether an object was public. An unguessable UUID is secrecy, not authorization: it cannot be revoked, never expires, and leaks through history, Referer headers, proxy logs and screenshots. Fix: new PRIVATE review-receipts bucket (verified private empirically, not from the flag); POST /reviews/receipt uploads there and returns an opaque key; GET /reviews/{id}/receipt authorizes author-or-moderator FIRST then mints a 300s signed URL; reviews.receipt_url -> receipt_key (migration 0023); ReviewOut exposes has_receipt instead of a locator; receipt_key_belongs_to() blocks attaching someone else's key. The migration also stripped the locator from all 675 review_versions snapshots - a second, independent leak found while tracing. 1 production receipt migrated to private storage and the public original neutralised then deleted. Regression suite: backend/tests/test_receipt_privacy.py. NOTE: applying the migration before deploying the code broke the production API for a few minutes - the deployed build still selected the dropped column. Migrate additively first next time.
